html:
"Cuman Khanates" is the map's label, for 1200, for the many tribes of the Cumans and Kipchaks, who held the steppe from the Danube to the lands beyond the Volga.

They never formed one state. Each tribe had its own khans, linked by kinship and alliances; see Cuman-Kipchak confederation. They raided the Rus principalities and Byzantium, but also traded with them and married into Rus princely families. The failed Rus campaign against them in 1185 is the subject of the Tale of Igor's Campaign.

In 1223 Cumans and Rus princes together lost to the Mongols at the Kalka River. The Mongols returned and conquered the steppe by 1241. Many Cumans fled to Hungary. Others were sold as slaves to Egypt, where they became soldiers of the Mamluk Sultanate; Baybars was one. Their speech became the common language of the Golden Horde.
sum: "Cuman Khanates" is the map's label, for 1200, for the many tribes of the Cumans and Kipchaks, who held the steppe from the Danube to the lands beyond the Volga.
